---
title: "Wrap Up and Feedback"

---

After an event, there are several important follow-up tasks to complete. These include sharing event materials, collecting feedback from participants, and communicating relevant information to instructors.

# Typical Post-Event Workflow

1. Publish the event materials (e.g., slides, recordings, repositories).
2. Send the formr feedback questionnaire to attendees and contributors.
3. Keep the survey open for approximately one week.
4. Generate the feedback report in formr once the survey period has ended.
5. Share the report with instructors and other relevant contributors.
6. Send certificates of completion, if applicable.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Recommendation

When sending feedback requests, keep the survey open for approximately one week and send the email as soon as possible after the event while participants' impressions are still fresh.
:::


## Dissemination of Event Materials

- [ ] Upload event materials (e.g., slides, recordings, handouts) to the appropriate repository, typically a subcomponent of the OSF repository "[Open Science Workshop Materials of the LMU Open Science Center](https://osf.io/zjrhu/overview)"
- [ ] If consent to record was obtained in advance, make recordings publicly available.
- [ ] Advertise the event materials and recordings on OSC mailing lists and social media channels, if appropriate (typically for large events like summer school).

## Creating feedback forms

Feedback should be collected from both attendees (quantitative) and event contributors (qualitative) whenever appropriate.

Example feedback forms are available as Gsheet in our Gdrive (see [Events](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1jrBRX6GLYdkQVerpMJIOsyrHhc0d6HWC)), to be used in **formr**: [https://formr.osc.lmu.de/](https://formr.osc.lmu.de/). 

See the [application chapter](https://lmu-osc.github.io/manual/osc-events/application.html) to learn more about formr. 
For example, here is a template for workshop feedback: [Workshop Feedback Form Gsheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1bOJMFQGDvXsULr8sb7aZ2Sn37lrIV7liAY7KummEfms/edit?gid=2110598566#gid=2110598566), [Workshop Feedback Form formR](https://surveys.osc.lmu.de/template-workshop-feedback/).

## Communication with Participants

- [ ] Send the feedback survey (usually a formr survey, see the [application chapter](application.qmd) to learn about formr and find some of our templates) to all registrants and ask them to complete it within one week.
- [ ] Include a link to the event materials repository (e.g., recordings, slides, handouts).
- [ ] Provide information about upcoming OSC and co-host events.

## Communication with Instructors

- [ ] Ask for qualitative feedback or a debrief call with all co-instructors 
- [ ] Send the feedback report (generated from the formr survey, see [event evaluation chapter](event-evaluation.qmd)) to instructors.

# Email Templates

## Email to Participants

The following examples can be adapted depending on the event, language, and available materials.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## German Wrap-Up Email Example 1
Liebe Teilnehmerinnen und Teilnehmer des Workshops „XX“,

vielen Dank für Ihr Interesse und Ihre Teilnahme! 

**Feedback:**
Wir möchten unsere Veranstaltungen stetig verbessern und laden Sie herzlich ein, uns in den kommenden ein bis zwei Wochen Ihr Feedback zu geben: *https://surveys.osc.lmu.de/XXX*.

**Material:**
Die Materialien zum Workshop finden Sie hier: *ZENODO LINK*.

**Weitere Trainings:** 
Besuchen Sie unser Website: [https://www.osc.lmu.de/](https://www.osc.lmu.de/) und insbesondere unsere Sammlung an Trainings-Ressourcen, die es ermöglichen sollen, offene und reproduzierbare Praktiken in unetrscheidlichen Disziplinen einfacher umzusetzen:

- ***[Self-Learning Catalog](https://www.osc.lmu.de/training/self-learning.html)*** - Praxisbezogene Tutorials zum Selbstlernen sowie Vorlesungsaufzeichnungen zu Open-Research-Methoden – darunter R für reproduzierbare Analysen,, Git/GitHub version control, Datenmanagement und -dokumentation, Datensimulation und Power-Analysen, Datenanonymisierung und vieles mehr
- ***[Research Cycle Handbook](https://www.osc.lmu.de/training/research-cycle-handbook.html)*** - Ein praxisorientierter Leitfaden für Forschende und Forschungsgruppen, um offene, verantwortungsvolle und reproduzierbare Praktiken Schritt für Schritt über den gesamten Projektlebenszyklus hinweg zu verankern
- ***[Educator Toolkit](https://www.osc.lmu.de/training/educator-toolkit.html)*** - Didaktische Schulungen und direkt einsetzbare Materialien, die Lehrende dabei unterstützen, ansprechende Trainings zu Open Research durchzuführen

**Bleiben Sie im Austausch!** Abonnieren Sie unsere LMU Open Science Center Mailingliste, um Ankündigungen zu Workshops, neuen  Tutorials, und Symposien zu erhalten: [https://lists.lrz.de/mailman/listinfo/lmu-osc](https://lists.lrz.de/mailman/listinfo/lmu-osc).

Herzliche Grüße,
*Name*


## German Wrap-Up Email Example 2

Liebe Teilnehmerinnen und Teilnehmer von „XX“,

vielen Dank für Ihr Interesse und Engagement!

📄 **Materialien**:
Das Material zum Event finden Sie auf OSF: *ZENODO Link*

Die Folien haben eine CC-BY-Lizenz und können gerne nachgenutzt werden.

📝 **Feedback**:
Wir laden Sie herzlich zu einer kurzen (2 Minuten) Umfrage zum Event ein: *https://surveys.osc.lmu.de/XXX*
Wie hat es Ihnen gefallen? Was würden Sie sich wünschen?

📢 **Informiert bleiben**:
Auf unserer Website oder über unsere Mailingliste erhalten Sie Ankündigungen zu zukünftigen Workshops und Symposien des LMU Open Science Center. 
Link zu unserer Mailingliste: [https://lists.lrz.de/mailman/listinfo/lmu-osc](https://lists.lrz.de/mailman/listinfo/lmu-osc).
Eine Liste **zukünftiger Open Science-Veranstaltungen** finden Sie hier:
[https://www.osc.lmu.de/events/](https://www.osc.lmu.de/events/).

🤝 **Mitglied werden**:
Als LMU-Angehörige können Sie sich auch aktiv an unseren Aktivitäten beteiligen, indem Sie Mitglied werden.

Viele Grüße,  
*Name*

## English Wrap-Up Email Example

Dear attendees of the „XX“ workshop,

Thank you for your participation!

**Feedback:**
In order to improve our events, please take 5 minutes to give us feedback by (1 or 2 weeks later): *https://surveys.osc.lmu.de/XXX*.

**Materials:**
You can find the workshop materials here: *ZENODO LINK*.

**Further training:** 
Visit our website: [https://www.osc.lmu.de/](https://www.osc.lmu.de/) and particularly, our training resource collections that aim to make the adoption of open and reproducible research practices easier and more scalable across disciplines:

- ***[Self-Learning Catalog](https://www.osc.lmu.de/training/self-learning.html)*** - free hands-on self-paced tutorials and lecture recordings on open research skills, including R for reproducible analyses, Git/GitHub for version control, data management and documentation, data simulation and power analyses, data anonymisation and many more
- ***[Research Cycle Handbook](https://www.osc.lmu.de/training/research-cycle-handbook.html)*** - practical guidance for researchers and research groups to embed open, responsible, and reproducible practices, step-by-step, across the full lifecycle of a project
- ***[Educator Toolkit](https://www.osc.lmu.de/training/educator-toolkit.html)*** - offering pedagogical training and ready-to-use materials to help educators deliver engaging training on Open Research

**Stay in touch!** You can subscribe to the LMU Open Science Center mailing list to receive announcements of workshops, new self-paced tutorials, and symposia here: [https://lists.lrz.de/mailman/listinfo/lmu-osc](https://lists.lrz.de/mailman/listinfo/lmu-osc).

Best wishes,

*Name*

## Carpentry workshop Wrap-Up Email

Subject: Certificate of Participation Software Carpentry

Dear <<Attendee>>,

Thank you for participating in the recent Software Carpentry Workshop. We appreciate your engagement and contributions during the sessions, and we hope the workshop has provided you with valuable insights and skills.
Attached to this email, you’ll find your certificate of participation.

Additionally, we would like to invite you to explore more self-paced tutorials offered by the LMU Open Science Center. These tutorials are designed to help you continue developing your computing skills and can be reused for your own teaching:

- Introduction to R: [https://lmu-osc.github.io/introduction-to-R/](https://lmu-osc.github.io/introduction-to-R/) 
- Version control with Git within RStudio:  [https://lmu-osc.github.io/Introduction-RStudio-Git-GitHub/](https://lmu-osc.github.io/Introduction-RStudio-Git-GitHub/) &  [https://lmu-osc.github.io/Collaborative-RStudio-GitHub/](https://lmu-osc.github.io/Collaborative-RStudio-GitHub/) 
- Quarto: [https://lmu-osc.github.io/introduction-to-Quarto/](https://lmu-osc.github.io/introduction-to-Quarto/) 
- Introduction to simulation of data analyses in R: [https://lmu-osc.github.io/Introduction-Simulations-in-R/](https://lmu-osc.github.io/Introduction-Simulations-in-R/) 
- Simulations for advanced power analysis in R: [https://lmu-osc.github.io/Simulations-for-Advanced-Power-Analyses/](https://lmu-osc.github.io/Simulations-for-Advanced-Power-Analyses/)  
- FAIR data management: [https://lmu-osc.github.io/FAIR-Data-Management/](https://lmu-osc.github.io/FAIR-Data-Management/)  
- Code publishing: [https://lmu-osc.github.io/code-publishing/](https://lmu-osc.github.io/code-publishing/)    
 
and more, on the LMU Open Science Center GitHub organisation:
[https://github.com/lmu-osc](https://github.com/lmu-osc) 


To receive announcements of future workshops and symposia organised by the LMU Open Science Center (see list of events here: [https://www.osc.uni-muenchen.de/events/index.html](https://www.osc.uni-muenchen.de/events/index.html)), please subscribe to the mailing list here:
[https://lists.lrz.de/mailman/listinfo/lmu-osc](https://lists.lrz.de/mailman/listinfo/lmu-osc)

Best wishes,

*Name*
:::


# Certificates

Some OSC events (e.g., Carpentry workshops, Summer Schools, or instructor training programs) may require certificates of completion.

Find templates for event certificates in the Google Drive folder here:

- [Templates Folder](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1HFmT0RPz6s7Z2DB13rbgREuWatF6I6-J?usp=drive_link)

Certificate templates should be adapted to the specific event, exported as PDF files, and sent to eligible participants after the event.
